colophon: Tiruchirrambalam: the holy Small Hall of Chidambaram, the closing salutation of Shaiva hymns.

lines.1: Whatever the color of gold, that is the color of his body, shining bright;
lines.2: whatever the color of lightning, that is the color of his falling locks; whatever the silver mountain's
lines.3: own color, that is the color of his great bull; and the color I turned when I saw him:
lines.4: whatever my color is, that color has become the Lord's.
lines.5: When I went with alms to see the Lord, 'What is this? Is she
lines.6: a madwoman in love with some ghoul?' So saying, before the foolish women,
lines.7: my mother dragged me away; and as I, alone, grew faint, that one with low-hanging locks
lines.8: said, 'Come, embrace me': and my sword-bright eyes flew open.
lines.9: Her eyes clouded, her bangles slipping, her garment coming loose,
lines.10: her bright throat and brow beaded with sweat, all for his bright konrai garland:
lines.11: 'She shames her womanhood, the girl has lost her mind,' they say, of a simple heart given
lines.12: to the Supreme One who stands and dances as the melodies are sung.
lines.13: The Supreme One: he went begging for alms, and drank the poison;
lines.14: from Brahma, seated on the many-petaled flower, he took a head, yet what he gives is great grace;
lines.15: he consented to Kama's arrow, yet the lady is the left half of his very body;
lines.16: his gracious household is his kin: the great ascetic with three eyes.
lines.17: 'The ascetic is himself the first cause of the world; all he has made
lines.18: is Shiva, wholly': those who say this will gain Shiva's world. 'The red one,
lines.19: he who rides the mighty bull, he who drank the poison from the midst of the sea,
lines.20: is Bhava': those who say this gain it too, here on this earth.
lines.21: Left side Vishnu, right side himself: on the left, tulasi; on the right, bright konrai
lines.22: garlands; on the left, cloth, on the right, hide; on the left, the discus, on the right, the deer;
lines.23: the left is dark, the right is red; lovely and fine, for him,
lines.24: on the left the dancing pot, on the right the kokkarai drum: so it is with our Dancer.
lines.25: Is it for a dance that he goes roaming? Is it to share out
lines.26: our bangles that he begs for alms? Is his body coral?
lines.27: Is it praise that he loves? Is it the chant of the gods
lines.28: that he has seen, this noble one with a garland in his locks?
lines.29: So that his devotees may rule the world as noble ones, the Lord to whom belong
lines.30: the datura, the snake, the moon, his mansion, his town, his goodness and unfailing glory,
lines.31: the Lord able to take anyone at all into his service, came, and
lines.32: as my own heart's companion, never leaving, he roams and dances with me.
lines.33: Though he wanders within my eyes and within my heart,
lines.34: his nature is hard to make known; yet dark is his throat
lines.35: where the ocean's poison sits, white his sandal paste of ash, and three eyes with his one form:
lines.36: he is kind, and he himself will graciously take up my many services.
lines.37: Bow at his feet; let singing and dancing be your music; with cool flowers
lines.38: adorn his feet, and hold to that ascetic as his servant;
lines.39: he who loves a cut hide for a garment and fills his body with ash will show you
lines.40: the good state of calm: why are you troubled, O my lonely heart?
lines.41: Heart sprouting new leaf, eyes brimming with tears, face blossoming,
lines.42: lovely red palms folded, bowing at his feet with all eight limbs,
lines.43: those able to adorn him with the flowers of their words: for them, the one of the low-hanging locks
lines.44: has cut away deceit and set aside, made ready, the great heaven.
lines.45: Those who rule the heavens, bathe in the heavenly Ganga, and go about crowned with honeyed flowers
lines.46: from the Nandana grove, and those who wrap themselves in rags
lines.47: and wander the forest till it wears them thin, begging: the first are servants of the gold-hued one
lines.48: with ash as white as milk, and the second are the false ones who are not.
lines.49: Speaking falsehoods, pampering this wasted body, going to door after door
lines.50: and stumbling: let us stop all that. Rise, O heart! Our Lord who dances in fire,
lines.51: the Lord who drank the poison that leapt from the sea: to reach his anklets, see,
lines.52: is the only use this body has, I tell you, here in this world.
lines.53: You who would rule the world, worship; you who would rule the heavens, bow; you who every day
lines.54: desire many things, think of him; you who long to be one with the Supreme,
lines.55: offer him fresh flowers from the good grove; you who would stand in the depths of hell,
lines.56: you who want your own ruin: go ahead and torment Hara's devotees!
lines.57: Water full of waves, fire, the sun, the earth, the moon, the sky, the wind,
lines.58: and the undying soul: gather round the Light that took these as its body!
lines.59: Though he lifted the mountain on his heads and strained, the demon of the bannered chariot, why, O why
lines.60: could he not bear the one toe that the deer-holding Lord let fall on him?
lines.61: As the First Cause sings a melody of love, and Kama's lovely arrow pierces through,
lines.62: who will hold up this girl who wilts, his garland her torment?
lines.63: Her eyes, sharp as spears arrayed for war, are veiled with a film of water, and her
lines.64: lovely breasts, flecked with golden pallor, lie covered as if with a golden cloth.
lines.65: Sitting, reaching, standing, roaming, lying down, drifting:
lines.66: give up this toilsome life, O heart, and go! The holy one with the young woman
lines.67: joined at his side, our Lord with the wounding trident: when we
lines.68: are set right, he himself will clear away our evil karma.
lines.69: Wretched with karma, I was chewed night and day by the five who stood over me;
lines.70: I grew sick of this clinging life; sick of it, I let it go; my karma too
lines.71: has ended; my heart has cleared; cutting away deceit, I have reached
lines.72: the feet of the three-eyed one of the spreading red locks, the Lord of the Vedas.
lines.73: His feet the earth, the fiery lights his eyes, the worlds his breath, the swelling
lines.74: ocean his garment, the high heaven his crest, the sky his body,
lines.75: the Vedas his face, the directions his shoulders, all the many tongues his song:
lines.76: what understanding is this! Beside him, O flowering vine, even a jewel's color loses.
lines.77: The bull upon his banner, the loincloth strip, a heron's feather,
lines.78: the anklets on his feet, the ash upon his chest, the five-hooded snake,
lines.79: the moon upon his crest, the fragrant blooming konrai, and the form
lines.80: of the three-leafed trident: they keep coming before my eyes, always.
lines.81: Against old age that is coming, and cruel disease, and Death, which day after day
lines.82: wage their war on me, I have no strength at all: grant that, smeared with ash, I may come
lines.83: and stand close beside you, O Brahmin who set upon your red locks
lines.84: the fire-mouthed snake, and the white moon it frightens.
lines.85: I bowed at the feet of the Brahmin, and bowing, as I stood longing to take into myself
lines.86: the light called true knowledge, he said, 'From today,
lines.87: this is the way.' 'And what is wealth?' I asked. Since then, O you whose tresses are lovely as bees,
lines.88: my thoughts, like yours, have let go of both sides.
lines.89: I have ended birth; I ride on joy; my heart has risen high;
lines.90: I have scorned this body; I will not go begging among others; this household too
lines.91: I have spurned; the elephant of the five senses, which breeds only blame,
lines.92: I have driven off with a shout; I have reached Shiva's feet: now I am wholly clear.
lines.93: I have not kept company with the wise, yet I set out to sing sweet verse;
lines.94: I lack bright words and meaning; and if I steal what others have said,
lines.95: the poets will not stand for it. O you who drank the ocean's poison,
lines.96: these are not worth taking, I know; but poor words though they are, graciously take them.
lines.97: You who, in your grace, drank the poison as it rose, and stood firm: while the throng of gods
lines.98: speak verses rich in meaning, I too have set about stringing poor words together,
lines.99: just as, when the great lovely moon appears to wipe away the stain of darkness, the firefly too, as if to say, 'That is fitting,'
lines.100: goes out undaunted to meet it, and spreads its glow.
lines.101: His body is like the rising sun; around that sun,
lines.102: his red locks are like its blazing, burning rays; beneath those locks,
lines.103: his throat is like the dark night sliding down; and below that dark night,
lines.104: my father's bright ash is like a drifting white cloud.
lines.105: Her breasts have not yet budded; her teeth have not all come in; she does not know the meaning of words;
lines.106: her hair cannot yet be tied up; yet listen: of the one whose red locks
lines.107: hold the great flood, whose throat is dark as a rain cloud, she smells of the fragrant konrai
lines.108: he wears on his body. I know nothing of what others say.
lines.109: Chanting the four Vedas rich in words, he roams all the worlds,
lines.110: his chest wreathed in fragrant konrai; on his spreading locks
lines.111: the wave-swelling Ganga, a sacred stream thick with foam, is held in,
lines.112: and the garland of skulls on our dark-throated Lord is like its rising bank.
lines.113: Dark-throated, wrapped in the flayed hide of an elephant, of spreading glory,
lines.114: the great one beyond the universe, the Lord who holds a little deer,
lines.115: the ancient one, Paramashiva, who cut off one of Brahma's heads,
lines.116: whose spear is wet with wounds, whose chest wears a close-strung garland: our holy one.
lines.117: The holy one; the one with the wounding spear; the one with the ocean's poison; with a garland of bones;
lines.118: with the eye set in his forehead; the First Cause; the one of the sky
lines.119: where the clouds move; the one whose hand is like the sky; he who, keeping time, makes Uma
lines.120: sing; the one whose songs are made of melody: the dancing Pashupati.
lines.121: Good ladies, a lord has come here seeking alms; and this one has
lines.122: a swift bull, has three eyes, has a stained throat,
lines.123: has a burning battle-axe, has a kokkarai drum, and the Lord's dance too;
lines.124: has locks that hold the moon; and has love, which he gives to the young women.
lines.125: Swallowing the kumkum paste on the broad breasts of the maiden here,
lines.126: so that every limb melts, he takes even the conch bangles from her palms:
lines.127: he with the crest where red-eyed snakes rear up in the waves of Lady Ganga,
lines.128: where the locks rest and the flowering moon stays: the Pandaranga dancer.
lines.129: The Pandaranga dancer came and said, 'Give me bali.' 'Give it to the sun,' I said.
lines.130: The one beyond the universe said, 'Annam!' 'That is Brahma's mount,' I said (annam is food, and also the swan).
lines.131: 'Bring your aiyam and pour it here,' he said. 'That is Kama, with his bannered chariot,' I said (aiyam pey, pour alms, is also ai ampu ey, shoot five arrows).
lines.132: When he said, 'Then it is settled here,' I understood what he meant.
lines.133: So that his close devotees may rule the world, without food or sleep,
lines.134: will the Lord's bull ever come to us? O you with small feet and long eyes like great spears,
lines.135: this girl with white teeth and red lips, for his garland of skulls, forever
lines.136: why does she waste away, till her waist is all but broken?
lines.137: Like butter melting in the fierce sun's heat, like wax at the mouth of a flame,
lines.138: love surges; like the palm of a hand, the night, heaven, and cruel Death,
lines.139: like fire rising in the roaring water: so, when the radiant three-eyed Lord
lines.140: came for his great alms, wearing fragrant konrai, the many lives melted.
lines.141: The teeth, the life, the half, the body, the head, the hide: of the Sun, of Death, of the Woman,
lines.142: of the Archer, of a Brahmin, of the Elephant, in that order, he plucked out, kicked away,
lines.143: embraced, burned, cut off, and flayed and took. Of his glory alone
lines.144: speak, and sing, and give praise, and the sorrows that surround us will perish.
lines.145: She grieves, she worships, she weeps, she droops, her garment and her girdle slipping;
lines.146: she wanders, she babbles, she laughs, she sighs hot breaths, bowing low again and again;
lines.147: she faints, she has to be sat down, she stretches and yawns: alas, like this
lines.148: she swoons, the bright-browed girl who became the servant of the Lord of Maraikkadu.
lines.149: This bright-browed girl's thinking is not good: when our father of the growing locks comes,
lines.150: she does not think to be shy; she goes with alms and laughs with longing,
lines.151: and plans to tend him: for Sthanu, whom even Brahma and Vishnu
lines.152: cannot reach, why does she pine night and day and sink so low?
lines.153: His locks hang low; on those locks is the Ganga; the locks where Lady Ganga
lines.154: lives; on those locks the moon; the locks where that child of a moon
lines.155: cuts its way; on those locks the swelling snake; the locks where that snake
lines.156: lives; and on those locks, the konrai: so it is with our great sage.
lines.157: O sage, O you of the fragrant blooming konrai, O fruit who took away
lines.158: my old age: but for your anklet-feet, I have no other refuge;
lines.159: from now on I will do no great penance; thinking only of the Five Syllables, so as to be set right,
lines.160: to whom else now should I tell the trouble that I, alone, endure?
lines.161: I will proclaim him; my head and my heart are his temple; by these I will perform
lines.162: my penance; pouring out the ghee called love, I will tend the flame, and with the lovely flowers of words
lines.163: I will raise him up; 'The Lord has come and is in my heart,' I will rise and spread the news abroad,
lines.164: and from now on I will speak only words of praise.
lines.165: A tongue that does not speak the name of the Light within light is no tongue, only fat;
lines.166: an ear his name does not enter is wood; a hand that does not trust and worship
lines.167: is stone packed with earth; a mind that does not think of him, a head that does not bow, a burden;
lines.168: and the other limbs, for such people, are lifeless things.
lines.169: A mountain of wealth, the great wide earth: if I got them without Shankara's grace,
lines.170: I would always hold them, in my heart, worse than poison; but if, by the grace of the one
lines.171: with the honey-dripping wild konrai, I were born a worm,
lines.172: I would always count it, for me, equal to the golden world of the gods.
lines.173: Can Kama's aim miss by even a little? Shankara, to whom the gods bow,
lines.174: with the cool lovely crescent in his locks and the conch earring, has come and
lines.175: dwells well within me; knowing this, yet to steal my bright complexion,
lines.176: Kama shoots at me night and day, never closing his eyes.
lines.177: 'First he destroyed Kama,' said that woman; this one said, 'Kala,
lines.178: Death with the fine garlanded chest, is the one he destroyed first,' and threw up her hands;
lines.179: when I asked, 'Whom did we destroy first, back then?', afraid of both women,
lines.180: the Brahmin could say neither 'yes' nor 'no.'
lines.181: 'This one is a Brahmin: where does he live?' I asked. 'At Arur,
lines.182: O you with sandal-smeared shoulders,' he said. 'A first-rate trickster,' I said.
lines.183: 'O you with a ball in your hand, that is true as well,' he said. 'So that Uma may know,
lines.184: tell me, you with the clustered garland,' I said: and he beat his drum.
lines.185: Some drum, many crowd around and roar; they tumble headlong, spring up,
lines.186: turn somersaults in the dance, frolic, sing, laugh, give frights,
lines.187: wheel in circles, go on strange wanderings: these are the goblins of Hara
lines.188: of Maraikkadu, ringed by vast groves where flowers sway and birds settle.
lines.189: O holy one with a goblin army, slanderous talk
lines.190: is rising against you to your shame: tell us, Lord, why
lines.191: Kama, who touched his arrow to make you fall in love with the young woman,
lines.192: was destroyed by the flower of your eye.
lines.193: To her breasts, like little caskets, he gave the color of the honeyed konrai flower;
lines.194: to her kohl-dark eyes he gave the flowing Ganga's stream; to her heart
lines.195: he gave the incomparable, gleaming datura of madness:
lines.196: O mother, what have you not received from our father, that you stand here crying out?
lines.197: The roaring water and the fire, the moon and the five-hooded snake,
lines.198: contemplative yoga and Uma, form and the formless, the tiger
lines.199: that looks for victory, and the deer, day and night, all of them
lines.200: have come together in the one who wears the monsoon konrai garland.
lines.201: For the one who has come together with her, many things: konrai loosened, a snake tied on,
lines.202: dancing in the forest by the water; not so much as a patch of ground
lines.203: his own, a homeless one: for the one with the blue throat,
lines.204: why is this girl so distraught, and wasting away?
lines.205: Her precious life is failing; distress grows; longing mounts;
lines.206: her conch bangles slip; on her breasts lies the sallow bloom;
lines.207: her tears pour down; her mouth is parched; her garment is gone: those who came,
lines.208: what are they saying now, to the three-eyed one of the four Vedas, her rightful one?
lines.209: The rightful one, first cause of old age and of the four Vedas, lord of the lovely
lines.210: shores of the seven seas, lord of the Kailasa mountain around, the Lord whose ancientness
lines.211: never fails, the Lord of eight qualities, who dwells in the hearts of those who praise him,
lines.212: the one with the snake: what more is there for us to say in praise of him?
lines.213: Chant his name; tell his many virtues; I have let you go:
lines.214: go after him, go and join him and set your life right;
lines.215: it will become great penance: whatever the great ascetic of the growing tawny locks
lines.216: has told you, take that and be done, from now on, O lovely one.
lines.217: This lovely one's face is the house of the five-arrowed god; in that house
lines.218: her arms are the festive arches, her broad hips his chariot, and her breasts
lines.219: the full ceremonial pots come down from ancient times: seeing all this, is it love that worships
lines.220: the feet of our First Cause with the twisted locks, or enmity, that she has in mind?
lines.221: She has nothing in mind, but listen: this lovely girl
lines.222: cannot last even one more day. From the holy one of the fine great bull, who fought until
lines.223: the unyielding yielded, bring the fresh swelling konrai now, and she will be well;
lines.224: if you do not bring it, the deep darkness will kill her.
lines.225: By his darkened throat, by night and day, by the mountain and the Vedas,
lines.226: by the precious fragrant konrai, by the mullai, by the snake from the anthill dancing,
lines.227: by the bright moon and the sky, by bearing the ocean's clear water,
lines.228: through his grace Hara has become every color, every one.
lines.229: What the Brahmin said came true: her waist-cloth and her bangles
lines.230: are gone; the kohl-dark water from her sword-like eyes has flowed down between her breasts,
lines.231: like the guiding line drawn for the saw in the love god's hand:
lines.232: so it is with our jeweled girl, who fell in love with the one of the many locks.
lines.233: Her jeweled, lovely breasts swell, and her waist is breaking with it;
lines.234: is it just talk, when she says 'Let these be bound up for me,' this faultless girl?
lines.235: She has fallen in love with the dark-throated one who dwells on Kalukkunram of the bamboo;
lines.236: her lovely fish-shaped eyes have stretched to meet her earringed ears.
lines.237: The one whose left side is joined to Uma, who dwells at Aiyaru,
lines.238: on whose many piled locks the colors show: bow to him, saying,
lines.239: 'His singing is the four Vedas, his leap was at Death, he burned the spreading cities
lines.240: and bathed in their ash, his red sandal paste: such is our Lord.'
lines.241: 'Are these alms? There is wealth enough here to feed one poor pilgrim, Sthanu,
lines.242: but your words are frightening, Pashupati, and your bull will leap at us!
lines.243: Holy one, loved by women whose hair falls to their shoulders, go away! Begging is wicked;
lines.244: even if you speak sweetly, we laugh; O sir, we are ashamed of you!'
lines.245: Walking without shame, there is no room for the good. As we write
lines.246: in noble, great Tamil, I will not forget; think of this, always,
lines.247: you with ornamented breasts: if the Dancer, our father with twisted locks, comes,
lines.248: I will not let him pass unseen; seeing him, I will not fail to beg his fragrant flower.
lines.249: Even if he gives me fragrant konrai, I will not embrace him; I will not let him near my garment;
lines.250: if he touches the flowers in my hair, I will be angry; if he touches my breasts, I will be undone;
lines.251: I will say, 'O you whose flower-feet the gods praise, this does not become you';
lines.252: and if he touches my bangled, flowerlike arms, I will swear by his holy name!
lines.253: Those who have renounced will give up the life they began for nothing,
lines.254: if their stilled desire does not rest in Hara; those not devoted to the three-eyed one of the red locks
lines.255: where six-legged bees curl up, here or anywhere,
lines.256: are many wretched ones, like crocodiles caught in a moat.
lines.257: On the right, the warrior's anklet; on the left, a woman's anklet; the snake on the right, and on the left,
lines.258: the one he has joined to himself; ash on the right, sandal paste on the left; fire on the right, a ball on the left; bones
lines.259: on the right, a gold garland on the left; a spear on the right, a ring on the left;
lines.260: on the right, locks where the water falls; on the left, cool tresses: so it is with Shankara.
lines.261: Shankara, with the conch earring: at his lotus feet,
lines.262: fold your lovely hands, worship, and become his servants, you devotees! The low deeds
lines.263: that Yama's servants do: when I hear even a little of them,
lines.264: my heart burns here, as if a thousand saws were cutting it.
lines.265: The Lord's locks are like a blazing fire; the water that surrounds them
lines.266: is like the ocean of milk the gods pour on that fire; in that water
lines.267: the gliding moon is like a boat; and the mighty snake is like
lines.268: the stout pole, plain to see, that pushes that boat along.
lines.269: When the snake breathes, it burns; when the lovely Ganga surrounds it, it grows cool;
lines.270: at the sulking of Uma, kuravam flowers in her hair, it wilts and melts; when the Lord
lines.271: whose glory his devotees praise touches it, it lights up earth and heaven:
lines.272: sorrow and joy both mingle in the white crescent our Lord wears.
lines.273: Is it to wear the sliver of moon? Is it to take alms and dance in fire?
lines.274: Is it to sing the verses of the Veda? Is it to be joined with bones and ash?
lines.275: Is it to embrace that stained throat? Is it to dance with the fierce-mouthed snake?
lines.276: Tell me, why does this girl, wanting something, follow Hara?
lines.277: Speak of the Lord; do him small services; let your eyes grow cool;
lines.278: be assured; clear your minds; hold fast to Shiva; quell your anger;
lines.279: cool your desire; cut away your grief: with these as your path,
lines.280: climb up, and live in the heavens as guests of the gods.
lines.281: The gods brought her down here; losing her modesty, she ran after the Lord,
lines.282: went by a path not fit for her, and, a deep woman of the waters, embraced him;
lines.283: that she should sit up there as the head wife of our Lord: what is this?
lines.284: Has Uma been given lodgings below her, that she lives there?
lines.285: Five dwell in it; it has nine gates and three humors;
lines.286: hidden bones and sinews, flesh, blood, and marrow,
lines.287: wrapped in shedding skin: this hut is useless. Go and reach
lines.288: the flower-feet of the one whose red locks hold the roaring clear water.
lines.289: To those who worshipped your garlanded feet with folded hands you gave the wide earth; but when I, a dog at your feet,
lines.290: a girl with eyes like a cut mango, worshipped you, you took my bangles! O you with the fragrant
lines.291: garland of konrai where the bees feed, to us you have shown two faces in one town,
lines.292: O mountain of virtue, who raised the fine fierce bull upon your banner!
lines.293: The one who lifted the mountain howled as his ears, eyes, mouths, and heads were crushed:
lines.294: that day he pressed him down and broke him, Shiva, given to those of true penance;
lines.295: while he stands there in the Hall, plain as an amla fruit in the palm, people go off
lines.296: and take up something else to recite, and fall into the pit of hell.
lines.297: Sunken eyes, a crooked gait, bent teeth, forked feet, a long lean waist,
lines.298: leafy ears like a tiger's, skin-bag breasts, whirlwind hair, a gaping mouth,
lines.299: bulging eyes, a wrinkled voice, a shrunken belly, twisted fingers:
lines.300: the dark-throated Lord's fearsome dance-stage is a home for such ghouls.
lines.301: The bell that will not stop, the anril bird, the south wind, Death itself, the moon, the lovely fire-
lines.302: arrows Kama shoots, all five: through the enmity of these she has grown faint;
lines.303: there is no one whose heart does not melt, but he will not melt, the one who loves
lines.304: the skulls of the gods and takes their bones: not for my sweet-spoken girl.
lines.305: He saw the slander spoken; he saw the sickness flare; he saw the conch bangles on my wrist
lines.306: break; he saw the anril bird tear at me; he saw the south wind
lines.307: whirl around my life; he saw my grief deepen; he saw my garment and girdle
lines.308: slip away: these are the thefts that the forehead-eyed Lord of Tillai has seen.
lines.309: The noblest one, who dwells within the hearts of those who have cast out
lines.310: the realm of deceit and learned to be his servants: on his long crest,
lines.311: wearing the white foam of the flooding waters, there is a snake that creeps
lines.312: to seize the wide crescent moon: take note of it!
lines.313: You came and aimed at the fine bangles this girl wore, and stole them:
lines.314: is it the fragrant vilva flower? Is it bone? Is it the konrai
lines.315: on your spreading locks? The hide you wear? The ash? Your broken bowl?
lines.316: O stained-throated one, what is it this little girl owes you?
lines.317: She owes nothing, but listen: we have seen how foolish
lines.318: this lovely girl has been. When our father with the crescent in his long locks came,
lines.319: to her who gave him room in her wide-open heart, he gave grief,
lines.320: like one who sits on a branch and cuts at its base.
lines.321: You cut off Brahma's head; you felled Jalandhara; like fire
lines.322: you seared the bodiless god and burned him, and the cities; and the water you packed onto your locks:
lines.323: these, I see, are your glories; but you who snatched this girl's few bangles,
lines.324: will this not be your disgrace? So I wonder.
lines.325: She is not as she used to be; the little girl does not know what is proper;
lines.326: her breath smells of guggul incense; her heart melts, and all over her body
